Instruction TTS.primary_help: Words you want the model to speak. Do not put voice directions here.
Instruction TTS.secondary_help: Describe voice character, tone, accent, or delivery. This description is used in the TTS prompt.
Instruction TTS.requirement: No audio required. Enter the words to speak and a voice description.
Instruction TTS.example: Target text: Welcome back. | Voice description: A warm, clear young female voice.
Instruction TTS.note: Use a short test sentence and a concise voice description. Automatic duration follows the target text. Base exposes sampling controls; Flash always uses 4 steps and CFG 0.
Instruction TTS.model_help: Base uses these sampling controls. Flash forces 4 steps and CFG 0 and uses a fixed time grid; the displayed NFE/CFG/sway values do not tune Flash. Seed still affects both variants. Task advice below describes listening checks, not benchmarked optimal settings.

control_help.seed: Seed selects the starting noise and can change the result. Try several seeds, then set control after generate to fixed before comparing settings. A larger seed is not better. Same seed alone does not guarantee identical audio across settings, model variants, or environments. Compare pronunciation, pauses, voice character, and delivery.
control_help.nfe_steps: Base: sampling steps, not repeated edit attempts. Start at 32; compare 48/64 if needed. More steps cost time and do not guarantee improvement. Flash always uses 4. Judge whether the words and requested voice style are clear without unnatural delivery.
control_help.cfg_strength: Base: extra guidance toward instruction and reference-audio conditioning. Start at 2; compare 1.5/2.5 with a fixed seed. Higher is not necessarily more accurate and can sound unnatural. CFG 0 still uses the instruction/reference; it disables the extra boost. Flash always uses 0. Judge whether the words and requested voice style are clear without unnatural delivery.
control_help.sway_sampling_coef: Base: distributes steps along the noise-to-audio process, not locations in the recording. 0 is evenly spaced; negative values concentrate steps earlier in sampling. Leave at -1 initially. Flash ignores this widget and uses its fixed time grid.
control_help.duration_mode: Automatic estimates length from target text. Manual uses target seconds and can change pacing or cause awkward timing; it is not an exact speaking-rate control.
control_help.generation_seconds: Automatic estimates length from target text. Manual uses target seconds and can change pacing or cause awkward timing; it is not an exact speaking-rate control.

Voice cloning.primary_help: New words to speak in the reference speaker's voice.
Voice cloning.secondary_help: Unused. Leave blank; a reference transcript or extra voice directions are not added to the cloning prompt.
Voice cloning.requirement: Connect clear reference speech from one speaker. Enter only the new words to speak.
Voice cloning.example: Target text: Hello, and welcome to today's program.
Voice cloning.note: Use clean, single-speaker reference speech. The reference supplies the voice; the first box supplies new words. Try different seeds for pronunciation variation, then fix the chosen seed.
Voice cloning.model_help: Base uses these sampling controls. Flash forces 4 steps and CFG 0 and uses a fixed time grid; the displayed NFE/CFG/sway values do not tune Flash. Seed still affects both variants. Task advice below describes listening checks, not benchmarked optimal settings.

control_help.seed: Seed selects the starting noise and can change the result. Try several seeds, then set control after generate to fixed before comparing settings. A larger seed is not better. Same seed alone does not guarantee identical audio across settings, model variants, or environments. Compare pronunciation and resemblance to the reference speaker, keeping the reference fixed.
control_help.nfe_steps: Base: sampling steps, not repeated edit attempts. Start at 32; compare 48/64 if needed. More steps cost time and do not guarantee improvement. Flash always uses 4. Listen for correct new words, speaker resemblance, and natural pacing; more CFG is not a voice-similarity slider.
control_help.cfg_strength: Base: extra guidance toward instruction and reference-audio conditioning. Start at 2; compare 1.5/2.5 with a fixed seed. Higher is not necessarily more accurate and can sound unnatural. CFG 0 still uses the instruction/reference; it disables the extra boost. Flash always uses 0. Listen for correct new words, speaker resemblance, and natural pacing; more CFG is not a voice-similarity slider.
control_help.sway_sampling_coef: Base: distributes steps along the noise-to-audio process, not locations in the recording. 0 is evenly spaced; negative values concentrate steps earlier in sampling. Leave at -1 initially. Flash ignores this widget and uses its fixed time grid.
control_help.duration_mode: Automatic estimates length from the NEW target text. Manual uses target seconds. Reference length is not the requested output length.
control_help.generation_seconds: Automatic estimates length from the NEW target text. Manual uses target seconds. Reference length is not the requested output length.

Speech text editing.primary_label: Edit request (one change at a time)
Speech text editing.secondary_label: Full source transcript (optional, duration estimate only)
Speech text editing.primary_help: One exact edit, such as Replace 'Los Angeles' with 'Florida'. Also supports Insert 'everyone' after 'Hello' and Delete 'um'.
Speech text editing.secondary_help: Optional full transcript of the CROPPED SOURCE audio, before the edit. Used only to estimate output duration; it is not a prompt or transcript correction.
Speech text editing.requirement: Connect ordinary spoken audio. Make one replacement, insertion, or deletion, using the exact original words.
Speech text editing.note: Prefer Base. Crop to the sentence around the edit with a little context. Match the original words exactly; use a longer unique phrase if they repeat. Set seed control to fixed for comparisons. Start with NFE 32, CFG 2, Sway -1; try a few seeds first, then compare NFE 48/64 or modest CFG changes one at a time. Extra instructions in box 2 are ignored. Check Final instruction and Run metadata.
Speech text editing.model_help: Base uses these sampling controls. Flash forces 4 steps and CFG 0 and uses a fixed time grid; the displayed NFE/CFG/sway values do not tune Flash. Seed still affects both variants. Task advice below describes listening checks, not benchmarked optimal settings.

control_help.seed: Seed selects the starting noise and can change the result. Try several seeds, then set control after generate to fixed before comparing settings. A larger seed is not better. Same seed alone does not guarantee identical audio across settings, model variants, or environments. Compare complete replacement, unchanged words, and voice continuity. Partial edits such as Florida Angeles may vary by seed.
control_help.nfe_steps: Base: sampling steps, not repeated edit attempts. Start at 32; compare 48/64 if needed. More steps cost time and do not guarantee improvement. Flash always uses 4. Listen for complete replacement, retained words, timing, and artifacts. Stronger CFG does not guarantee that the whole phrase is replaced; try a longer phrase with context first.
control_help.cfg_strength: Base: extra guidance toward instruction and reference-audio conditioning. Start at 2; compare 1.5/2.5 with a fixed seed. Higher is not necessarily more accurate and can sound unnatural. CFG 0 still uses the instruction/reference; it disables the extra boost. Flash always uses 0. Listen for complete replacement, retained words, timing, and artifacts. Stronger CFG does not guarantee that the whole phrase is replaced; try a longer phrase with context first.
control_help.sway_sampling_coef: Base: distributes steps along the noise-to-audio process, not locations in the recording. 0 is evenly spaced; negative values concentrate steps earlier in sampling. Leave at -1 initially. Flash ignores this widget and uses its fixed time grid.
control_help.duration_mode: Always automatic from source speech and the edit. Box 2 accepts the full original CROPPED transcript for the length estimate only. Manual target seconds and connected Float are ignored. Check resolved duration.
control_help.generation_seconds: Always automatic from source speech and the edit. Box 2 accepts the full original CROPPED transcript for the length estimate only. Manual target seconds and connected Float are ignored. Check resolved duration.
